initial.article: NOTES ON INTERACTION / 07The interface should remember the hand.Useful movement begins with a simple promise: the surface will answer when someone acts upon it.That answer does not need spectacle. Often the strongest response is small enough to feel inevitable, arriving exactly where attention already rests.Motion can describe a relationship before language has time to explain it.Timing matters because sequence matters. A transition should preserve the cause of change while revealing its result.The final test is not novelty. It is whether the experience becomes easier to understand and trust.FIELD NOTE 07 / END
